Definition: from G1260; discussion, i.e. (internal) consideration (by implication, purpose), or (external) debate:--dispute, doubtful(-ing), imagination, reasoning, thought.
BiblicalUsage: Thoughts are the reasonings of the heart, and the Gospels show them at work in friend and enemy alike. Jesus perceives the thoughts of the Pharisees, evil thoughts proceed from the heart to defile a man, and Paul tells the Philippians to do all things without disputing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe my thoughts are never private from God. He reads them as plainly as words, and the question is whether they are turned toward Him or curled inward on myself.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
